title: boomtime — Daily Review
description: DOMAIN-perspective daily review of boomtime: what the app DID, not whether its pods are healthy (that is Ops > App). Job runs by kind and outcome, backlog and pipeline flow, the domain outcomes that landed (wakatime imports, Audible/Hardcover book sync, label artwork), and the warning/error pile to read through. SOURCES: boomtime emits NO Prometheus metrics of its own, so every domain panel is built on its structured JSON slog output in Loki (namespace=boomtime); backlog and pipeline panels come from the KEDA scaler and RabbitMQ queue metrics in Mimir. KNOWN GAPS: per-request heartbeat counts, per-project/per-language attribution, and catalyst-go-jobs run durations are not observable today — they live only in Postgres.

list.name: proc
list.label: Process
list.description: Which boomtime process to read logs from: the always-on server, the always-on AMQP image worker, or the KEDA ScaledJob drain pods that run the heavy DB job kinds. Default All covers every one of them and excludes the co-located postgres/rabbit/dragonfly pods.

list.name: kind
list.label: Job kind
list.description: catalyst-go-jobs kind (the registry key a handler is registered under). Default All is the regex .+, so a NEW kind shows up here without editing the dashboard — it just won't be in the picker until it is added to this variable's list.

list.name: bucket
list.label: Bucket
list.description: Width of each bar/sample in the over-time panels. auto keeps roughly 30 buckets across the selected range.

panels.title: Coding heartbeats accepted
panels.description: catalyst-waka ingest: accepted POSTs to /heartbeats and /heartbeats.bulk over the dashboard range. NOTE this counts REQUESTS, not individual heartbeats — a bulk POST carries many and boomtime logs no per-request heartbeat count (see the gaps note in the dashboard description).

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |~ "heartbeats" | json | msg = "http request" | method = "POST" | path =~ `/api/v1/users/current/heartbeats(\.bulk)?` | status < 400 [$__range]))

panels.title: Health / workout samples accepted
panels.description: catalyst-health ingest: accepted POSTs to /workouts, /workouts.bulk, /health_samples and /health_samples.bulk (the boomtime-watch Apple Watch extension). Zero here means the health domain sent nothing in the range.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |~ "workouts|health_samples" | json | msg = "http request" | method = "POST" | path =~ `/api/v1/users/current/(workouts|health_samples)(\.bulk)?` | status < 400 [$__range]))

panels.title: Job runs completed
panels.description: catalyst-go-jobs runs that reached a handler and returned nil ("jobs: done").

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: done" | json | msg = "jobs: done" | kind =~ "$kind" [$__range]))

panels.title: Job runs failed
panels.description: Runs that exhausted every attempt and were recorded terminally failed. Each one is a piece of domain work that did NOT happen today.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: failed (attempts exhausted)" | json | kind =~ "$kind" [$__range]))

panels.title: Retries scheduled
panels.description: Runs that errored but had attempts left, so they were re-queued with a linear backoff (attempt x 30s, capped at 10m). Healthy in small numbers; a rising count means something downstream is flaky.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: retry scheduled" | json | kind =~ "$kind" [$__range]))

panels.title: Warnings + errors logged
panels.description: Every WARN/ERROR record from the boomtime processes over the range — the size of today's log-review pile. The feed itself is at the bottom of this dashboard.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |~ `"level":"(WARN|ERROR)"` [$__range]))

panels.title: Job runs — what ran, and how it went
Job runs by kind
panels.description: Terminal catalyst-go-jobs outcomes (done + failed) bucketed over time and stacked by kind. This is the 'what did boomtime work on' view: each bar is the mix of domain work that completed in that bucket. Colors are pinned per kind, so a kind keeps its hue when the others drop out.

targets.expr: sum by (kind) (count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |~ "jobs: done|jobs: failed" | json | msg =~ `jobs: (done|failed.*)` | kind =~ "$kind" [$bucket]))

panels.title: Job kinds over the range
panels.description: Per-kind tally of completed / retried / failed runs across the whole range. The table is also the colorblind-safe reading of the stacked chart beside it — identity by name, not by hue.

targets.expr: sum by (kind) (count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: done" | json | msg = "jobs: done" | kind =~ "$kind" [$__range]))
sum by (kind) (count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: retry scheduled" | json | kind =~ "$kind" [$__range]))
sum by (kind) (count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: failed (attempts exhausted)" | json | kind =~ "$kind" [$__range]))

panels.title: Job outcomes over time
panels.description: The same runs split by OUTCOME rather than kind: completed, retried, failed. Status colors are reserved (green/amber/red) and each series is named in the legend, so the state never rides on hue alone.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: done" | json | msg = "jobs: done" | kind =~ "$kind" [$bucket]))
sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: retry scheduled" | json | kind =~ "$kind" [$bucket]))
sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "jobs: failed (attempts exhausted)" | json | kind =~ "$kind" [$bucket]))

panels.title: Job failures and retries — with the reason
panels.description: Every terminal failure and scheduled retry, newest first, reformatted to kind / job id / attempt / error. This is the panel to read when the failed-runs stat above is non-zero.

targets.expr: {namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |~ "jobs: failed|jobs: retry scheduled|jobs: no handler" | json | msg =~ `jobs: (failed.*|retry scheduled|no handler for kind)` | kind =~ "$kind" | line_format "{{.kind}}  job={{.id}}  attempt={{.attempt}}{{.attempts}}  {{.msg}}  {{.err}}"

panels.title: Backlog and pipeline — what is still waiting
Heavy-job backlog now
panels.description: Rows in the Postgres jobs table that are queued AND due for the heavy kinds (avatar-render, label-image) — read straight off the KEDA postgres scaler that decides whether to schedule a drain pod. This is domain work boomtime has accepted but not yet done.

targets.expr: max(keda_scaler_metrics_value{scaledObject="boomtime-jobs"})

panels.title: Image-job queue depth
panels.description: Messages sitting ready on the boomtime.image-jobs RabbitMQ queue — label artwork requested but not yet rendered.

targets.expr: sum(rabbitmq_queue_messages_ready{namespace="boomtime", queue="boomtime.image-jobs"})

panels.title: Image jobs in flight
panels.description: Unacked messages — image renders a worker has picked up and not yet finished. A number that never falls means a wedged consumer.

targets.expr: sum(rabbitmq_queue_messages_unacked{namespace="boomtime", queue="boomtime.image-jobs"})

panels.title: Image workers attached
panels.description: RabbitMQ consumers on boomtime.image-jobs. Zero with a non-empty queue is the classic stall: work is queued and nothing is draining it.

targets.expr: sum(rabbitmq_queue_consumers{namespace="boomtime", queue="boomtime.image-jobs"})

panels.title: Backlog trend
panels.description: Both backlogs on one axis (they are the same unit — items of undone domain work). A sawtooth is healthy: work arrives, a worker drains it. A staircase that only climbs is the thing to catch on a daily review.

targets.expr: max(keda_scaler_metrics_value{scaledObject="boomtime-jobs"})
sum(rabbitmq_queue_messages_ready{namespace="boomtime", queue="boomtime.image-jobs"})
sum(rabbitmq_queue_messages_unacked{namespace="boomtime", queue="boomtime.image-jobs"})

panels.title: Image-job flow
panels.description: Publish vs deliver rate on boomtime.image-jobs. Delivered tracking published means the pipeline keeps up; a persistent gap is what fills the backlog panel to the left. Redelivered rising means work is being retried rather than completed.

targets.expr: sum(rate(rabbitmq_queue_messages_published_total{namespace="boomtime", queue="boomtime.image-jobs"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum(rate(rabbitmq_queue_messages_delivered_total{namespace="boomtime", queue="boomtime.image-jobs"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum(rate(rabbitmq_queue_messages_redelivered_total{namespace="boomtime", queue="boomtime.image-jobs"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Image render time
panels.description: How long an image job actually took to execute, from the imagejobs consumer's own timing (slog encodes the Go duration as nanoseconds; this panel converts to seconds). This is the ONLY job duration boomtime currently logs — the catalyst-go-jobs kinds emit no timing at all.

targets.expr: max(quantile_over_time(0.95, {namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "imagejobs: execute done" | json | unwrap dur [$bucket])) / 1000000000
max(quantile_over_time(0.50, {namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "imagejobs: execute done" | json | unwrap dur [$bucket])) / 1000000000

panels.title: Wakatime heartbeats imported
panels.description: Heartbeats pulled in by a completed catalyst-waka bulk import (the "imported" total on each "import completed" record), summed over the range. Empty when no import ran — imports are user-triggered, not periodic.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "import completed" | json | unwrap imported [$__range]))

panels.title: Audible library items backfilled
panels.description: Items walked by a completed catalyst-books Audible backfill. This is the one-time history pull, distinct from the periodic forward sync below.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "audible backfill complete" | json | unwrap libraryItems [$__range]))

panels.title: Books newly finished
panels.description: Titles the Audible forward sync saw flip to finished in the range — the domain event that drives a Hardcover push.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "audible forward: newly finished" | json | unwrap count [$__range]))

panels.title: Pushed to Hardcover
panels.description: Finished books successfully written out to Hardcover. Note the deployment may be in DRY-RUN (BOOM_HARDCOVER_DRYRUN) — check the warning feed at the bottom, where the dry-run banner is logged on every boot.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "hardcover: pushed finished book" [$__range]))

panels.title: Label-image generation runs
panels.description: Outcome of each labelimages sweep: images generated, candidates skipped because artwork already existed, and entries that failed. Stacked, so bar height is the size of the sweep.

targets.expr: sum(sum_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "labelimages: run complete" | json | unwrap generated [$bucket]))
sum(sum_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "labelimages: run complete" | json | unwrap skipped_existing [$bucket]))
sum(sum_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |= "labelimages: run complete" | json | unwrap failed [$bucket]))

panels.title: Domain outcome feed
panels.description: The plain-language record of what boomtime accomplished: imports finishing, Audible backfills and forward syncs, Hardcover pushes, avatars and label artwork saved. Read this top-to-bottom for the daily recap.

targets.expr: {namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |~ "import completed|audible backfill complete|audible forward: newly finished|hardcover: pushed finished book|labelimages: run complete|labelimages: saved|avatar regen: saved" | json | line_format "{{.msg}}  {{.user}}{{.id}}"

panels.title: Top warnings and errors
panels.description: Distinct WARN/ERROR messages over the range, most frequent first. Work down this list; the raw feed beside it has the detail.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (level, msg) (count_over_time({namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |~ `"level":"(WARN|ERROR)"` | json [$__range])))

panels.title: Warnings and errors (live)
panels.description: Every WARN and ERROR record from the boomtime processes, newest first. Expand a line for the full structured payload (job ids, error strings, upstream response bodies).

targets.expr: {namespace="boomtime", app_kubernetes_io_name=~"$proc"} |~ `"level":"(WARN|ERROR)"` | json | line_format "{{.level}}  {{.msg}}  {{.err}}"
